rules: ONE in-progress at a time. Evidence before pass. Cross-contract features carry BOTH sides' proof in one entry (docs/spec/init-monorepo-contract/04-harness-binding.md). A design-tier entry may not go in-progress before its docs/design/ doc is approved (docs/spec/init-harness/06-design-first.md). New entries MAY carry an optional acceptance array (AC ids/text); when present, evidence names which AC each command proved (docs/spec/init-harness/02-artifacts-and-templates.md 2.2) — entries below predate it and were recorded as-built, so they have none. pass is terminal here; release readiness lives in docs/spec/init-release.

Return body {lateFee?, damageFee?, depositRefund?, note?} (ints ≥0) → payment rows via PaymentRecorderPort/Adapter writing the payments-owned TABLE directly (payments context is schema-only; same boundary trick as DressLookupAdapter; one transaction per settlement; zero/omitted amounts NOT recorded; the note rides on every row). features.title: Business outcomes survive the HTTP boundary: outcome bodies + error envelope across BE, contract, apps/fe and apps/qr-admin (ADR 0001; closes BE gap #6 + FE gap #8)

BE: libs/exceptions gains BusinessOutcomeException + ErrorDetail + ApiErrorResponseDto; the global filter renders the two shapes only; 9 command controllers map each returned domain error to its own snake_case code with a typed payload (dressIds / currentStatus / dressCode) and declare @ApiResponse 422 with a per-slice outcome DTO. AC3: the EXCLUDE race is translated by rental.repository -> RentalItemsOverlapError and converted in create-rental.service back to the SAME rejected_dress_unavailable outcome (re-queried dressIds). AC4: login/refresh reject as outcomes so 401 means only 'guard rejected the access token'. Contract re-emitted, both clients regenerated (idempotent re-run verified by md5). FE: src/api/errors.ts is now the single mapApiError seam (outcome vs fault); the three features/*/lib/is-conflict-error.ts files are deleted; dresses/rentals/today/auth render one designed state per code with new vi+en keys (parity checked by pnpm --filter fe arch). qr-admin: src/api/errors.ts replaces error-message.ts. After committing the regenerated layer, contract:check, the arch freshness item and a full `bash init.sh` are green. Real-browser runtime proof: `pnpm --filter fe e2e` (vi happy path vs migrated+seeded Postgres, BE :3000, Vite :5173) passes — sign-in, create-dress, booking, pickup, return-and-settle and the payments dialog all work on the new wire shapes; its board locators were scoped to the run's own rows so a non-empty database no longer breaks it.

AC2: every technical fault returns { error: { code, message, details?, correlationId } }; ValidationPipe 400s carry details[] per field

AC2: a test provokes the same constraint by concurrent requests (race) and by a raw INSERT that bypasses the application, proving the DB — not the app — is the enforcer

AC4: pnpm --filter be test:e2e exists and runs the suite against a fresh compose/CI Postgres; CI has a postgres service and runs it

features.title: Auto-computed late fee at return, with owner-only waiver (FR-RENT-09)
features.evidence: 2026-08-09: design gate — use-case spec drafted at docs/design/rentals/settle-late-fee.md + contract check on the draft shape (2 blockers, 2 major, 2 minor); held at todo because the fee formula and waiver authority are business rules the lane forbids inventing. 2026-08-10: the shop owner answered (spec §6) — 200,000 VND per dress per day flat, no grace, no cap; the cleaning buffer does NOT count as late; only owner may charge less and must give a reason; the meaning change of `lateFee` accepted in place. Spec flipped to approved, then implemented and re-synced to as-built (§7). AC1: the rule is a pure value object (domain/late-fee.value-object.ts, 8 unit tests incl. buffer-irrelevance and month boundaries) reached through RentalEntity.lateFeeQuote; reference day is shopToday() in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh so money never depends on the VPS clock. AC2: omitting lateFee charges the suggestion — proven by unit test and by e2e (payments row = 400,000 for 2 days × 1 dress). AC3: a staff waiver answers 403 { status: forbidden, reason: late_fee_waiver_requires_owner, suggestedLateFee, submittedLateFee } with the rental still `out` and no payments row; an owner waiver without a note answers 422 rejected_waiver_note_required; with a note it records the reduced amount — all three over real HTTP in test/late-fee.e2e-spec.ts, plus staff charging exactly or more still succeeds. AC4: the dialog reads GET /rentals/:id/late-fee, shows 'Trễ 3 ngày · 2 váy → đề xuất 1.200.000 ₫' in an aria-live banner, pre-fills the field, disables submit until the quote lands, keeps both waiver rejections in place (field errors, note focused), and falls back to manual entry when the quote fails — 4 new vitest cases. Gates: be 95 unit + 30 e2e, fe 57, qr-admin 13, root check/lint/arch/build green; contract regenerated for both clients in the same commit. Side fix found while testing: lib/format.ts read the app i18n singleton, so money formatted en-style under test while the text was vi — it now reads <html lang>.
acceptance: AC1: daysLate and the suggested fee follow the formula approved in spec §6 Q1-Q3 (cleaning buffer excluded), computed as a pure function - same inputs, same result
AC2: submitting the return without lateFee charges the suggested fee; payments records the amount actually charged
AC3: charging LESS than suggested is refused for staff with the named 403 outcome forbidden + reason late_fee_waiver_requires_owner (payload carries suggested + submitted), and accepted for owner
AC4: the return dialog shows days late and the suggested amount BEFORE submit, pre-filled and editable, with a fallback when the quote call fails

features.title: Playwright happy path runs in CI against the real stack (browser proof stops being manual)
features.evidence: AC1: `pnpm --filter fe e2e` now starts what it needs — apps/fe/playwright.config.ts declares two webServers (`pnpm --filter be build && start` on :3000, checked via /api/v1/dresses answering 401; `pnpm build && vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort`) — proven by a cold run against only `docker compose up -d` + migrate + seed: 1 passed (18.2s), and again with CI=1 (reuseExistingServer off): 1 passed (17.1s). The browser now exercises the PRODUCTION build, not the dev server, so the shipped artifact + service worker are covered; `vite.config.ts` gained the matching `preview.proxy` for /api. AC2: new `e2e` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml — own postgres service, playwright install --with-deps chromium, `pnpm --filter be migrate`, `pnpm --filter be seed` (SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD=changeme, the pair the spec signs in with), then `pnpm --filter fe e2e`; YAML parsed, 5 jobs. NOT yet observed on a real GitHub run — first push proves it. AC3: with E2E_BASE_URL set, `webServer` is undefined — run against a dead port emitted 0 `[WebServer]` lines and failed in seconds instead of booting Nest/Vite. AC4: the html reporter is configured (open: never), and the same failing run produced BOTH apps/fe/playwright-report/ and apps/fe/test-results/<test>/trace.zip, which is exactly what the job uploads on failure. acceptance: AC1: `pnpm --filter fe e2e` starts the stack it needs itself (BE :3000 + the FE production build) and passes on a machine that has only a migrated + seeded database running
AC2: the same command runs as a CI job on every push/PR, with its own postgres service, and fails the build when the happy path fails
AC3: a developer who already runs the stack by hand keeps the documented flow — E2E_BASE_URL means 'I own the servers', and nothing is started for them

features.title: The return dialog states the money: standard deposit out to the client, refund pre-filled, every amount read back grouped
features.evidence: UI/UX review finding P0: the return dialog asked staff to type a seven-digit refund from memory while the customer waited, with no thousand separators and no arithmetic on screen — the only screen in the app that moves real cash. AC1: `RentalDressDto` gained `depositAmount` (BE `DressSnapshot` + `DressLookupAdapter` now select `deposit_amount`; both read projections pass it through), documented in the DTO as the catalog STANDARD deposit and explicitly NOT what was collected — no deposit is recorded at booking time. Contract re-emitted and both clients regenerated in this commit. AC2: opening the dialog pre-fills `depositRefund` with `depositTotal − suggestedLateFee` (5.000.000 − 1.200.000 = 3.800.000 proven by a 2-dress vitest case; 3.000.000 in full when on time). AC3: a live reference block states `Cọc chuẩn N váy: X` and `Trừ phí F → hoàn lại khách Y`, recomputing as fees are typed (damage fee 500.000 → 2.500.000) and adding `Bạn đang nhập …` when the field disagrees with that arithmetic. AC4: each amount field renders its digits back grouped through `FormDescription`, which the shadcn form primitives already wire into `aria-describedby`. Gates: be 95 unit (today-board projection spec now asserts the deposit rides along per dress), fe 59 (+2 new cases, 1 rewritten for the pre-fill), qr-admin 13, root check/lint green, both builds green; `pnpm arch` freshness item red until this commit lands the generated layer, as designed. Assumption recorded for the shop owner: pre-filling `deposit − fees` encodes the deduction convention observed in `apps/be/scripts/smoke.sh` (lateFee 200.000 + refund 2.800.000 on a 3.000.000 deposit) and in the Playwright happy path; the field stays editable and the arithmetic is on screen, but the convention itself was never approved in writing the way the late-fee rules were.
acceptance: AC1: the standard deposit of each dress reaches the board and list reads, labelled as a reference rather than as a recorded fact
AC2: opening the return dialog pre-fills the refund with the standard deposit minus the suggested late fee, and the field stays editable
AC3: a live block shows deposit, fees deducted and the resulting refund, and says so when the typed refund differs
AC4: every amount field reads its own digits back with thousand separators, associated with the input for assistive tech

features.title: The new-rental form answers 'which dress is the problem' — per-dress availability before submit, and the rejection points at the named dresses
features.evidence: UI/UX review findings #4 and #5: `rejected_dress_unavailable` carries `dressIds` by design (ADR 0001 §3) and the form threw the payload away, leaving one sentence about 'some dress' for staff to resolve by removing dresses one at a time; and the picker searched the catalog with no idea of the dates already typed above it. FE-only — no API changed. AC1: each SELECTED dress now runs `GET /dresses/:id/availability` for the form's range (own child component per row, so the hook count stays static), rendering a `Còn trống` / `Vướng lịch` badge plus `Váy này bận tới hết <blockedUntilDate>` — the cleaning-buffer date, which is exactly the case staff cannot deduce; proven by a vitest case whose seeded booking ENDS before the asked range and still blocks it through the buffer. AC2: search results are deliberately NOT checked — one query per keystroke per row for an answer nobody asked for; recorded in the component. AC3: on rejection the form reads `dressIds` through a shape-checking helper and marks only those rows (destructive tint + per-row reason); proven with 2 dresses where only the second is refused — exactly one flag, and it sits in that row's `<li>`. All three dress rejections (`unavailable` / `retired` / `notFound`) get their own row copy. AC4: the flag is dropped as soon as the selection or either date changes, since it answered for the old range — proven by a case that changes the start date and watches the flag disappear. Gates: fe 63 tests (+4 new), check/lint/arch green, be untouched (95), qr-admin 13.
acceptance: AC1: a dress that cannot serve the typed date range says so in its row, with the date it is busy until, before anything is submitted
AC2: the availability check covers chosen dresses only, never the search results
AC3: a rejection marks exactly the dresses the server named, each with the reason for that code
AC4: a rejection is cleared as soon as the dates or the selection change

features.title: Dress photos appear where staff choose dresses — catalog list and the rental picker
features.evidence: UI/UX review finding #6: a dress shop recognises stock by sight, and `photoUrls` (shipped with catalog/manage-dress) was visible only on the detail page — the catalog list and the picker where dresses are actually CHOSEN were text-only. FE-only, no API change: the list DTO already carries the links. AC1: new kernel component `components/media/photo-thumbnail.tsx` renders the first photo at row size or a neutral icon; it is decorative (`alt=""`) because the dress code sits next to it in every caller, so announcing it again is noise. AC2: a dead link degrades to the placeholder instead of a broken-image glyph — the links are staff-pasted third-party URLs, so that is an ordinary state; the failed URL is remembered rather than a boolean flag, so a row that later receives a different photo tries again. AC3: wired into the catalog table (leading column, `sr-only` header) and into BOTH picker lists (search results and the chosen dresses, the latter through a new optional `photoUrl` on `SelectedDress`). Gates: fe 64 tests (+1 asserting the img src for a dress with a photo and its absence for one without — asserted on the DOM, since a decorative image has no `img` role), check/lint/arch green.
acceptance: AC1: the catalog list and both picker lists show the dress photo at row size, or a neutral placeholder
AC2: a broken photo link renders the placeholder, never a broken image
AC3: the thumbnail adds nothing for a screen reader, since the dress code is already text next to it
